'''Bryant:''' {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} {{legend0|#6674de|60–70%}} {{legend0|#584cde|70–80%}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[David Pryor]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Tim Hutchinson]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsAR}} The '''1996 United States Senate election in Arkansas''' was held on November 5, 1996. Incumbent Democratic U.S. Senator [[David Pryor]] decided to retire. Republican [[Mike Huckabee]] initially ran for the open seat and won the Republican primary. However, he withdrew after taking the governorship and was subsequently replaced by [[Tim Hutchinson]]. Hutchinson went on to win the general election, becoming the first Republican to win a U.S. Senate seat in Arkansas since [[Reconstruction era|Reconstruction]] in 1872 and the first Republican to ever be popularly elected in the state. Hutchinson would later lose re-election in [[2002 United States Senate election in Arkansas|2002]] to David Pryor's son [[Mark Pryor|Mark]]. In the [[1996 United States presidential election in Arkansas|concurrent presidential election in Arkansas]], Democrat [[Bill Clinton]] — a native Arkansan who had previously served as governor — defeated Republican [[Bob Dole]]. To date, this is the last time that Republicans flipped a Senate seat in a presidential election year despite losing the state in the concurrent presidential election. == Democratic primary == === Candidates === * Bill Bristow, attorney * [[Winston Bryant]], [[Arkansas Attorney General]]{{cite web |title=AR US Senate - D Primary 1996 |url=https://www.ourcampaigns.com/RaceDetail.html?RaceID=7263 |website=OurCampaigns |access-date=14 August 2020}} * Lu Hardin, [[Arkansas State Senate|state senator]]{{cite news |last1=Lancaster |first1=Bob |title=Who are these guys? |url=https://arktimes.com/news/cover-stories/1996/05/17/who-are-these-guys |access-date=14 August 2020 |work=Arkansas Times |date=17 May 1996}} * Sandy McMath, attorney and son of former governor [[Sidney Sanders McMath]] * Kevin Smith, [[Arkansas State Senate|state senator]] ====Withdrew==== * Jay Bradford, state senator from [[Pine Bluff, Arkansas|Pine Bluff]], Senate Majority Whip, and Democratic nominee for U.S. representative in 1994 (endorsed Bryant) * [[Pat Hays]], mayor of [[North Little Rock, Arkansas|North Little Rock]] (endorsed Bryant){{cite web | url=https://lotsofbook.club/sl-S1B8Q-D7256/signup-blitz/#/z=Vr80NNEL4txAlxAmqvkJ1e/variation=default/q=nlr+mayor+patrick+hays+reflects+24+years+office.html/s1=lp/s2=/s3=/s4=/s5=/source_id=b41e5f8b-cada-5dc2-403f-936aad3512b3/project=w68GsX/mh_offer_id=/dp=SdjDVIdJaN3OJfareddsVV/m=/c_color=/source=Referral/software=Browser/domain=cdn.bkfd4.club/ | title=Access Books, Audiobooks, Magazines and More! }} ====Declined==== * [[Mike Beebe]], then a state senator in the [[Arkansas General Assembly]] and a future [[governor]]; explored a bid but didn't announce{{cite web | url=https://www.sfgate.com/news/article/Senate-Demos-Lining-Up-To-Retire-Pryor-the-3035570.php | title=Senate Demos Lining up to Retire -- Pryor the Fifth | date=21 April 1995 }} * [[Mack McLarty]], 17th [[White House Chief of Staff]]{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/politics/1995/04/22/pryor-makes-it-official-hes-leaving-the-senate/ff2b700d-5e98-4e22-80a7-4986fd4dcdf5/ |title=Pryor Makes It Official, He'S Leaving The Senate |newspaper=The Washington Post |date=1995-04-22 |accessdate=2022-06-13}}{{cite journal | url=https://www.csmonitor.com/1995/0501/01012.html | title=Democrats See 'Solid South' Slipping Away | journal=Christian Science Monitor | date=1 May 1995 }} (endorsed McMath){{cite web | url=https://www.armoneyandpolitics.com/mack-mclarty-2/ | title=Mack the Nice: Thomas F. "Mack" McLarty, III | date=29 April 2019 }} * Lamar Pettus, associate justice of the [[Supreme Court of Arkansas]] (ran for chief justice of the Arkansas Supreme Court){{cite web | url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2021/apr/28/other-days/ | title=Other days | date=28 April 2021 }} Arkansas Attorney General Winston Bryant and Arkansas State Senator Lu Hardin finished in the top two in the primary, and Bryant narrowly defeated Hardin in the runoff. === Primary results === {{Election box begin no change | title = Democratic primary results }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | candidate = [[Winston Bryant]] | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 129,328 | percentage = 39.99% }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | candidate = Lu Hardin | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 71,889 | percentage = 22.23% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Bill Bristow | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 58,093 | percentage = 17.96% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Sandy McMath | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 42,303 | percentage = 13.08% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Kevin Smith | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 21,774 | percentage = 6.74% }} {{Election box end}} === Runoff results === {{Election box begin no change | title = Democratic runoff{{cite web |title=AR US Senate - D Runoff 1996 |url=https://www.ourcampaigns.com/RaceDetail.html?RaceID=7264 |access-date=14 August 2020}} }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | candidate = [[Winston Bryant]] | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 87,564 | percentage = 52.44% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Lu Hardin | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 79,411 | percentage = 47.56% }} {{Election box end}} == Republican primary == === Candidates === * [[Mike Huckabee]], [[lieutenant governor of Arkansas]] ===Results=== Huckabee was unopposed for the nomination. ===Huckabee withdrawal=== Although Huckabee won the Senate nomination unopposed in the May primary, he abandoned his Senate bid when Governor [[Jim Guy Tucker]] resigned from office and he became [[governor of Arkansas]].{{cite news | url=http://www.cnn.com/ALLPOLITICS/1996/news/9605/31/huckabee/index.shtml | title=AllPolitics - Wanted: A Senate Candidate - May 31, 1996 | website=[[CNN]] }} ===Replacement selection=== Following Huckabee's withdrawal, several candidates announced their interest in running: * John E. Brown, state senator from [[Siloam Springs, Arkansas|Siloam Springs]] * [[Jay Dickey]], U.S. representative from [[Pine Bluff, Arkansas|Pine Bluff]] * [[Tim Hutchinson]], U.S. representative from [[Fort Smith, Arkansas|Fort Smith]] * Julia Hughes Jones, former [[Arkansas State Auditor]] (1980—1994){{cite web | url=https://encyclopediaofarkansas.net/entries/julia-hughes-jones-5909/ | title=Encyclopedia of Arkansas }}{{cite web | url=https://encyclopediaofarkansas.net/media/julia-jones-campaign-material-8583/ | title=Encyclopedia of Arkansas }} The main candidates were Dickey and Hutchinson, but in light of a potential impasse, some compromise candidates were floated: * [[Ed Bethune]], former U.S. representative from [[Searcy, Arkansas|Searcy]] and nominee for Senate in 1984{{cite news | url=http://www.cnn.com/ALLPOLITICS/1996/states/AR/news/0606.shtml | title=AllPolitics - Arkansas GOP Gets Top State Office but Loses Top Senate Candidate | website=[[CNN]] }} * Steve Luelf, former state senator and candidate for governor in 1994 * [[Sheffield Nelson]], chair of the Arkansas Republican Party and gubernatorial nominee in 1990 and 1994 * [[Tommy F. Robinson]], former U.S. representative and candidate for governor in 1990 * [[Frank D. White]], former governor of Arkansas (1980–1982) On June 11, White, Nelson, and Bethune all endorsed Hutchinson. Shortly thereafter, Jones and Dickey withdrew and endorsed Hutchinson. Brown also withdrew his candidacy to seek Hutchinson's open House seat, which he lost to Hutchinson's younger brother [[Asa Hutchinson]] in a special convention. Hutchinson was ratified as the nominee by the Arkansas Republican State Committee.{{cite news | url=http://www.cnn.com/ALLPOLITICS/1996/states/AR/news/0618.shtml | title=AllPolitics - Bryant, Hutchinson Contend for Open Senate Seat in Arkansas | website=[[CNN]] }} ==Results== Hutchinson won election to the U.S. Senate, receiving just over 5% more of the vote than his opponent Bryant. This was despite incumbent U.S. President [[Bill Clinton]] being [[1996 United States presidential election in Arkansas|re-elected]] by a 17-point margin in his home state of Arkansas, though the state had begun to trend more Republican at the time. {{Election box begin no change | title=1996 United States Senate election in Arkansas{{cite web|url=https://www.ourcampaigns.com/RaceDetail.html?RaceID=160|title=Our Campaigns - AR US Senate Race - Nov 05, 1996|website=www.ourcampaigns.com}}{{cite web|url=https://www.ourcampaigns.com/RaceDetail.html?RaceID=3|title=Our Campaigns - AR US Senate Race - Nov 05, 2002|website=www.ourcampaigns.com}}}} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | party = Republican Party (United States) | candidate = [[Tim Hutchinson]] | votes = 445,942 | percentage = 52.70% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | party = Democratic Party (United States) | candidate = [[Winston Bryant]] | votes = 400,241 | percentage = 47.30% }} {{Election box total no change | votes = 846,183 | percentage = 100.0% }} {{Election box gain with party link no change | winner = Republican Party (United States) | loser = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{Election box end}} == See also == * [[1996 United States Senate elections]] == Notes == {{notelist}} == References == {{reflist}} {{Arkansas elections}} {{United States elections, 1996}} [[Category:1996 United States Senate elections|Arkansas]] [[Category:United States Senate elections in Arkansas|1996]] [[Category:1996 elections in Arkansas]]
